questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Slow down and keep going if no cars are coming
Come to a complete stop, then go only when it is safe
Stop only if a police officer is present
questions.explain: Texas law requires a full stop at a stop sign unless an officer or a traffic signal tells you to go. After stopping, you yield to traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.

questions.q: You approach an intersection with this sign. What must you do?
options: Slow down, give the right-of-way to cross traffic, and stop if needed
Always come to a full stop before entering
Speed up to merge ahead of cross traffic
questions.explain: At a yield sign you must slow to a reasonable speed and let vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard go first. You stop only when safety requires it.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may enter only to make a U-turn
The road ahead is closed for repairs
Do not drive into this road or ramp; traffic on it comes toward you
questions.explain: This sign is posted where a driver could wrongly enter a one-way road, a divided highway, or a ramp. Entering would put you against the flow of traffic.

questions.q: You see this sign facing you after turning onto a road. What does it tell you?
options: You are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or ramp and must get out of that direction safely
You missed your exit and should back up on the shoulder
The road ahead has a detour
questions.explain: A WRONG WAY sign backs up the DO NOT ENTER sign and is placed farther along a one-way roadway. Seeing it means you are heading against oncoming traffic.

questions.q: What does this sign tell you about the street it points along?
options: Only one lane is open ahead
Vehicles may travel only in the direction of the arrow
You may turn only once on this street
questions.explain: ONE WAY signs mark streets where traffic is allowed to move in one direction only, shown by the arrow.

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
options: Left turns
Changing lanes
U-turns
questions.explain: A red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow is a movement prohibition sign: turning around (a U-turn) is not allowed here.

questions.q: What does this sign at an intersection mean?
options: Left turns are not allowed
Left turns are allowed only on a green arrow
The left lane ends ahead
questions.explain: The red circle and slash over a left-turn arrow is a movement prohibition sign that bans left turns from this approach.

questions.q: This sign is posted at a signal where you want to turn right. The light is steady red. What should you do?
options: Stop, then turn right when the way is clear
Stop and wait for a signal that lets you go
Turn right without stopping if no one is in the crosswalk
questions.explain: Texas normally allows a right turn on red after stopping, but a posted sign can prohibit it. With this sign you must wait for a signal that allows the turn.

questions.q: A railroad crossing has only this sign, with no lights, gates, or flagger. What does Texas law require?
options: Always stop, even if no train is near
Nothing special; trains must stop for cars at unmarked crossings
Yield to any train close enough to be a hazard, and stop if safety requires it
questions.explain: At a crossing marked only with crossbucks, you must give trains the right-of-way, go at a reasonable speed, and stop when needed for safety.

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign warn you about?
options: A railroad crossing is ahead
A rest area is ahead
Road repairs are ahead
questions.explain: The round Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign is placed ahead of railroad crossings to give you time to look, listen, and slow down.

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Move into the left lane
Slow down; the road curves to the right ahead
Turn right at the next intersection
questions.explain: This yellow warning sign shows a curve to the right ahead. Texas law requires a reduced, appropriate speed when approaching and going around a curve.

questions.q: What does this sign warn drivers on the main road about?
options: The road ahead is divided by a median
Your lane ends and you must exit
Traffic from another roadway may be merging into your lane ahead
questions.explain: The Merge sign warns that two roadways join ahead, so watch for entering vehicles and adjust your speed or position.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The number of lanes is reduced ahead, so drivers in the ending lane must merge
A new lane is being added on the right
Passing is allowed on the right
questions.explain: The Lane Ends sign warns that the number of lanes in your direction drops ahead. Drivers in the ending lane must merge into the remaining lane.

questions.q: What does this warning sign tell you?
options: A railroad crossing with lights is ahead
There is a traffic signal ahead that you may not be able to see yet
Traffic signals ahead are not working
questions.explain: The Signal Ahead sign is used before a traffic signal that is hard to see from far away, so you can be ready to stop.

questions.q: What should you expect after passing this sign?
options: A school bus stop
A toll booth
A stop sign ahead, so be ready to stop
questions.explain: The Stop Ahead sign warns of a stop sign that may not be visible in time, giving you room to slow down.

questions.q: You are leaving a divided highway and see this sign. What does it mean?
options: Oncoming traffic will now share the road with you, with no median between
Two lanes of traffic go your direction ahead
You may pass on either side
questions.explain: The Two-Way Traffic sign warns that a divided road is changing to a two-lane road with traffic in both directions.

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A hiking trail is nearby
People may be crossing the road ahead
Pedestrians are not allowed on this road
questions.explain: The pedestrian warning sign alerts you to a place where people may cross or walk in the road, so slow down and watch for them.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road may become unexpectedly slippery, so slow down when it is wet
Winding road ahead
Do not use your brakes
questions.explain: This sign warns of a surface that can be slippery. Texas law calls for a reduced speed when weather or road conditions create a hazard.

questions.q: This sign is at the front of a median. What does it tell you?
options: Turn right at the median
The right lane is closed
Pass only to the right of the median or obstruction
questions.explain: The Keep Right sign is used where traffic must go only to the right side of a roadway feature such as a median island.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Do not stop on the roadway
Passing other vehicles is not allowed here
Pedestrians may not pass
questions.explain: The DO NOT PASS sign is a regulatory sign that backs up no-passing pavement markings where passing is unsafe.

questions.q: This pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of a two-lane road. What does it mark?
options: The start of a zone where passing is not allowed
The end of a no-passing zone
A left-turn lane ahead
questions.explain: The NO PASSING ZONE pennant is placed on the left side of the road where a no-passing zone begins.

questions.q: What does this orange sign tell you?
options: A detour is required for all vehicles
The road is closed ahead
You are approaching a work zone, so expect workers, equipment, or lane changes
questions.explain: Orange is the color for temporary traffic control. The ROAD WORK sign is placed in advance of a work area to warn of obstructions or restrictions.

questions.q: What should you be ready to do after this sign?
options: Speed up to get through the work zone quickly
Slow down and follow the directions of a flagger who may stop you
Change lanes to the left
questions.explain: The Flagger sign is placed ahead of a spot where a person is controlling traffic. Be prepared to stop and follow the flagger's signals.

questions.q: What does this blue sign indicate?
options: A hospital that is open 24 hours a day, every day
A hotel nearby
A highway rest area
questions.explain: Blue signs show road-user services. The Hospital sign may only be used for facilities that operate around the clock, seven days a week.

questions.q: This sign is next to the left-turn signal. The light is a steady green ball. What does it mean?
options: You may turn left only on a green arrow
Oncoming traffic must stop for you
You may turn left, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explain: On a circular green you may turn left, but you must yield to vehicles lawfully in the intersection and to pedestrians. The sign reminds you that the turn is not protected.

questions.q: In Texas, this emblem on the back of a vehicle means the vehicle:
options: Is carrying hazardous materials
Is designed to travel at 25 mph or less
Is about to make a wide turn
questions.explain: Texas requires a slow-moving-vehicle emblem on vehicles built to travel at 25 mph or less, so other drivers can see them early and slow down.

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign warn you about?
options: A playground is closed
Children may be playing in a park
You are near a school, where children may be crossing or nearby
questions.explain: The pentagon-shaped School sign warns that you are approaching a school area, a school zone, or a school crossing.

questions.q: Which color is used for signs in road work and other temporary traffic control zones?
questions.explain: Orange is the national color for temporary traffic control, such as work zones.

questions.q: Which color is used for signs that guide you to services such as gas, food, or a hospital?
questions.explain: Blue is reserved for road-user services guidance, tourist information, and evacuation routes.

questions.q: Which color is used on school, pedestrian, and bicycle warning signs?
questions.explain: Fluorescent yellow-green marks warnings about pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, school buses, and schools.

questions.q: Which sign color means stop or that something is prohibited?
questions.explain: Red is used for stop or prohibition, as on STOP, YIELD, and DO NOT ENTER signs.

questions.q: Which sign color points you to parks and other recreational or cultural areas?
questions.explain: Brown signs give guidance to recreational and cultural interest areas.

questions.q: Which color on signs shows direction guidance and movements that are permitted?
questions.explain: Green indicates permitted movements and direction guidance, such as highway guide signs.

questions.q: The round shape is reserved for only one warning sign. Which one?
questions.explain: A circle is used only for the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign, which tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.q: Which of these is a regulatory sign, telling you a rule you must obey?
questions.explain: Regulatory signs give notice of traffic laws; DO NOT PASS is one. The yellow diamonds are warning signs about conditions ahead.

questions.q: You face a steady green light (a full circle, not an arrow). What does Texas law allow?
options: Go straight only; turns need an arrow
Go straight or turn, but yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to pedestrians
Go straight or turn, and pedestrians must wait for you
questions.explain: A circular green lets you go straight or turn unless a sign forbids it. You must still yield to vehicles lawfully in the intersection and stop for pedestrians lawfully crossing.

questions.q: What does a steady yellow traffic light tell you?
options: Speed up to beat the red light
Pedestrians have the right-of-way
The green movement is ending and a red light is coming
questions.explain: A steady yellow warns that the movement allowed by green is ending or that red is about to show, so prepare to stop if you safely can.

questions.q: You are stopped at a steady red light. When may you turn left on red in Texas?
options: From a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
Never
Whenever there is no oncoming traffic
questions.explain: After a full stop and yielding, Texas allows a left turn on red only when both streets are one-way and the turn is otherwise allowed. A posted sign can forbid it.

questions.q: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: Slow down and go through with caution
Treat it like a stop sign: stop, then go when it is safe
Stop and wait until it turns green
questions.explain: A flashing red means stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or edge of the intersection, then proceed under the same rules as a stop sign.

questions.q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: You may proceed, but only with caution
Come to a full stop
The signal is broken and you must turn around
questions.explain: Facing a flashing yellow, you may go through the intersection or past the signal only with caution.

questions.q: You reach an intersection where the traffic lights are completely dark because of a power outage. What must you do?
options: Go through if the road looks clear, since no signal applies
Yield only to vehicles on your right
Stop as if the intersection had a stop sign
questions.explain: Texas law says a signal showing no light at all is treated like a stop sign (this does not cover freeway ramp meters or pedestrian hybrid beacons).

questions.q: A police officer directing traffic waves you through a red light. What should you do?
options: Wait for the light to turn green
Follow the officer's directions
Honk and wait for the officer to step aside
questions.explain: You must obey traffic-control devices unless a traffic officer, police officer, or escort flagger directs you otherwise.

questions.q: A green arrow is lit for your lane. What does it allow?
options: Moving only in the arrow's direction, while still yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk and traffic lawfully in the intersection
Moving in any direction
Moving in the arrow's direction without watching for anyone
questions.explain: A green arrow lets you enter carefully in the direction shown. You must still yield to pedestrians in an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

questions.q: A red plaque reading ALL-WAY is mounted under a STOP sign. What does it tell you?
options: Cross traffic does not have to stop
Every approach to this intersection has a stop sign
You may turn any direction without stopping
questions.explain: The ALL-WAY plaque is placed under each STOP sign at intersections where traffic on every approach must stop.

questions.q: Unless a sign shows otherwise, the Texas speed limit on a street in an urban district (other than an alley) is ___ mph.
questions.explain: Texas sets a prima facie limit of 30 mph on urban district streets that are not alleys.

questions.q: In an urban district in Texas, the speed limit in an alley is ___ mph unless posted otherwise.
questions.explain: The prima facie limit for an alley in an urban district is 15 mph.

questions.q: Outside an urban district, the Texas speed limit on a US or state-numbered highway is ___ mph unless a different limit is posted.
questions.explain: For passenger vehicles, Texas law sets 70 mph on US and state-numbered highways outside urban districts.

questions.q: Outside an urban district, on a highway that is not numbered by Texas or the United States, the limit is ___ mph unless posted otherwise.
questions.explain: Texas sets 60 mph on highways outside urban districts that do not carry a state or US number.

questions.q: When driving on a Texas beach, the speed limit is ___ mph.
questions.explain: State law sets a 15 mph limit on beaches.

questions.q: On a 60 mph road, you approach a stopped police car with its lights on and cannot move out of the lane next to it. You must slow to at least ___ mph below the posted limit.
questions.explain: If you cannot vacate the lane closest to the vehicle, Texas requires slowing to 20 mph below a posted limit of 25 mph or more.

questions.q: On a section of state highway designed for it and approved after an engineering study, the Texas Transportation Commission may set a speed limit of up to ___ mph.
questions.explain: Texas law lets the commission set a limit of up to 85 mph on highway sections designed for that speed, after an engineering and traffic investigation.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: 65 mph is the recommended speed only
65 mph is the minimum speed
65 mph is the maximum lawful speed under good conditions
questions.explain: A black-on-white Speed Limit sign is a regulatory sign showing the highest speed allowed there. Going faster is evidence your speed is unlawful.

questions.q: You pass this sign during heavy rain with poor visibility. Is driving 65 mph legal?
options: Yes, any speed up to the posted limit is always legal
Not if 65 mph is faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
Only if you turn on your hazard lights
questions.explain: Posted limits apply unless a special hazard calls for a slower speed. You may never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions, including weather.

questions.q: You get a speeding ticket after passing this sign, in a work zone posted with a speed limit sign, while workers are present. What happens to the fine?
options: The minimum and maximum fines are doubled
The fine stays the same
The fine is waived if no one was hurt
questions.explain: In a construction or maintenance work zone with workers present, Texas doubles both the minimum and maximum fine. For speeding, the zone must be marked with a sign showing the speed limit.

questions.q: What is the basic speed rule in Texas?
options: Always drive at the posted limit
Never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
Keep up with the fastest traffic
questions.explain: Texas law forbids driving faster than is reasonable and prudent given the existing conditions and hazards.

questions.q: Under Texas law, a driver must control speed as needed to:
options: Arrive on time
Save fuel
Avoid hitting any person or vehicle lawfully on or entering the road
questions.explain: Drivers must control their speed to avoid colliding with others who are on or entering the highway lawfully.

questions.q: Texas law requires a reduced speed when you are:
options: Approaching and crossing an intersection or a railroad crossing
Driving on a straight, empty highway
Merging onto a freeway
questions.explain: Approaching and crossing an intersection or railroad grade crossing is one of the situations where the law calls for an appropriate reduced speed.

questions.q: You are approaching the top of a hill and cannot see over it. What does Texas law require?
options: Speed up so you do not lose momentum
Drive at an appropriate reduced speed
Move to the left lane
questions.explain: The law lists approaching a hill crest as a situation that calls for a reduced, appropriate speed, because you cannot see what is ahead.

questions.q: On a narrow, winding road, you should:
options: Drive at the highest speed allowed for the road
Use the center of the road
Reduce your speed
questions.explain: Traveling on a narrow or winding roadway is one of the conditions where Texas law requires a reduced speed.

questions.q: In Texas, driving faster than a prima facie speed limit is:
options: Evidence that your speed is not reasonable and prudent, and is unlawful
Always legal if traffic is light
Only a warning, never a ticket
questions.explain: A speed over the prima facie limit is treated as evidence that the speed is unreasonable and unlawful.

questions.q: Can you get a speeding ticket in Texas while driving below the posted limit?
options: No, the posted limit is always a safe speed
Only at night
Yes, if a special hazard such as fog or ice made that speed unsafe
questions.explain: Posted and statutory limits are lawful only when no special hazard requires a slower speed. You must still drive at a reasonable and prudent speed.

questions.q: For speed limits, Texas defines an "urban district" as an area along a highway where buildings are less than 100 feet apart for a distance of at least:
options: 100 yards
One-quarter mile
One mile
questions.explain: An urban district is territory along a highway with business, industrial, or residential buildings spaced less than 100 feet apart for at least one-quarter mile.

questions.q: How do Texas speed limits differ between day and night?
options: Night limits are always 5 mph lower
They are the same day and night
Night limits apply only on rural highways
questions.explain: Texas requires any entity that sets or changes a speed limit to use the same limit for daytime and nighttime.

questions.q: What speed limit applies to a pickup truck (a light truck) in Texas?
options: The same limit as a passenger car at that time and place
10 mph below the car limit
The truck limit posted for large trucks
questions.explain: Texas law gives light trucks, such as pickups, the same speed limits as passenger cars.

questions.q: Before the Texas Transportation Commission can change a state highway speed limit, what must it rely on?
options: A vote of drivers who use the road
The speed limits of neighboring states
An engineering and traffic investigation
questions.explain: The commission may change a prima facie limit only after an engineering and traffic investigation shows the existing limit is unreasonable or unsafe.

questions.q: When does a new speed limit set by the Texas Transportation Commission take effect?
options: When signs giving notice of the new limit are put up
On January 1 of the next year
As soon as it is published in a newspaper
questions.explain: A limit declared by the commission becomes effective when the commission erects signs showing the new limit.

questions.q: Besides a regular limit, the Texas Transportation Commission may declare a separate speed limit for which condition?
options: Holiday weekends
Wet or inclement weather
Tourist season
questions.explain: The commission may declare a reasonable and safe speed for wet or inclement weather, meaning rain, ice, or snow that makes the road hazardous.

questions.q: A Texas city wants to change the speed limit on one of its streets. What is the highest limit it may set?
options: 65 mph
85 mph
75 mph
questions.explain: A city may change limits by ordinance based on an engineering and traffic investigation, but it may not set a limit above 75 mph.

questions.q: Is it legal in Texas to drive so slowly that you hold up the normal flow of traffic?
options: No, unless the slower speed is needed for safety or to obey the law
Yes, driving slowly is always safe
Yes, as long as you stay in the left lane
questions.explain: Texas prohibits driving so slowly that you impede normal and reasonable traffic, except when reduced speed is needed for safety or required by law.

questions.q: A highway has a posted minimum speed limit. When may you drive slower than it?
options: Whenever you are looking for an exit
Only when necessary for safe operation or to obey the law
Any time you are in the right lane
questions.explain: Where signs give notice of a minimum speed, you may not drive slower except as necessary for safe operation or to comply with the law.

questions.q: Which vehicle is exempt from Texas speed limits?
options: A delivery truck running late
A driver taking a sick friend to the hospital
An ambulance responding to an emergency call
questions.explain: The speed rules do not apply to authorized emergency vehicles responding to a call, police patrols, or a physician or ambulance responding to an emergency call.

questions.q: After a lowered speed limit in a state highway work zone, how will you know the speed limit once the zone ends?
options: A sign at the end of the zone shows the speed limit after the zone
You return to 70 mph automatically
You keep the work zone speed until the next city
questions.explain: An entity that lowers a work zone limit on the state highway system must post a sign at the end of the zone showing the limit that applies afterward.

questions.q: TxDOT posts a temporary lower speed limit at a highway maintenance site. Which limit must you obey there?
options: The usual higher limit, because temporary signs are only advice
The temporary lower limit
Whichever limit other drivers are following
questions.explain: A temporary limit set for a maintenance site is enforceable like any other limit and overrides limits that would allow a higher speed.

questions.q: In Texas, who sets the reduced speed limit in a school crossing zone?
options: The school principal
The State Board of Education
The local authority, such as the city or county
questions.explain: Texas defines a school crossing zone as a reduced-speed zone designated by a local authority to help children cross safely while the reduced limit applies.

questions.q: A sign reads SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT 20 WHEN FLASHING. When does the 20 mph limit apply?
options: While the attached yellow lights are flashing
Only on weekends
All day, every day
questions.explain: The School Speed Limit When Flashing sign marks a reduced school speed zone that is in effect while its beacons flash.

questions.q: You see a yellow REDUCED SPEED LIMIT AHEAD sign. What does it mean?
options: You may ignore the next speed limit sign
The road ahead is closed
A lower speed limit starts at the next Speed Limit sign, so prepare to slow down
questions.explain: This warning sign gives advance notice of a lower limit. It must be followed by a Speed Limit sign showing the same speed where the zone begins.

questions.q: A yellow plaque showing "35 MPH" is mounted under a curve warning sign. What does it tell you?
options: The minimum speed through the curve
The advisory speed recommended for the curve
The speed limit for trucks only
questions.explain: An Advisory Speed plaque supplements a warning sign to show the speed recommended for that condition, based on an engineering study.

questions.q: You are on a farm-to-market road outside an urban district, and no speed limit is posted. What is the limit for a passenger car?
options: 60 mph
55 mph
70 mph
questions.explain: Farm-to-market and ranch-to-market roads count as state-numbered highways, so the 70 mph limit outside urban districts applies.

questions.q: You reach an intersection with no signs or signals at the same moment as a car on the cross street to your right. Who should go first?
options: You, because you are going straight
The car on your right
Whichever driver is going faster
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled intersection Texas law requires you to yield to a vehicle that is in the intersection or approaching from your right closely enough to be a hazard.

questions.q: You are driving on a street that ends at a T-intersection with no signs or signals. What must you do?
options: Yield to traffic on the through street
Expect through-street traffic to yield to you
Honk and turn without stopping
questions.explain: When your road ends at an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield to vehicles on the other road that are in or close to the intersection.

questions.q: Your unpaved road meets a paved road at an intersection with no traffic control. Who has the right-of-way?
options: You, because you arrived first
Whoever is turning right
Drivers on the paved road
questions.explain: A driver coming from an unpaved road must stop and yield to vehicles on the paved road that are in or near the intersection.

questions.q: You are on a two-lane road approaching an intersection with a divided highway, and there is no sign or signal. What must you do?
options: Slow down but keep the right-of-way
Stop and yield to vehicles on the divided highway
Yield only to trucks on the highway
questions.explain: Texas law requires a driver on a one- or two-lane road to stop and yield at an uncontrolled intersection with a divided highway or a road with three or more marked lanes.

questions.q: You come to an intersection where the traffic light is completely dark because of a power failure. What should you do?
options: Stop as if there were a stop sign, then go when it is safe
Drive through at normal speed
Slow down and go without stopping if no one is coming
questions.explain: A traffic signal that shows no light in any signal head must be treated like a stop sign: stop, then proceed when you can do so safely.

questions.q: You want to turn left, and the red car is coming straight toward you through the intersection. What should you do?
options: Turn quickly before it arrives
Turn because left turns have priority on green
Wait and let the oncoming car go first
questions.explain: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

questions.q: You face this sign and there is no stop line or crosswalk. Where should you stop?
options: Exactly 50 feet before the sign
At the point nearest the cross road where you can see approaching traffic
In the middle of the intersection
questions.explain: Without a stop line or crosswalk, you stop at the spot closest to the intersecting road from which you can see traffic coming.

questions.q: This intersection is controlled by a stop sign. Where must you stop?
options: At the white stop line
Past the crosswalk, at the edge of the cross street
Anywhere you can see traffic, even inside the crosswalk
questions.explain: When a clearly marked stop line is present, Texas law requires you to stop at that line.

questions.q: At a stop sign there is a marked crosswalk but no stop line. Where do you stop?
options: On top of the crosswalk
Just past the crosswalk
Before entering the crosswalk
questions.explain: If there is no stop line, you must stop before you enter the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection.

questions.q: What does Texas law require when you approach this sign?
options: Stop completely every time, even when no one is near
Slow down, and stop if needed, to let cross traffic go first
Speed up to merge ahead of other traffic
questions.explain: At a yield sign you must slow to a reasonable speed and give the right-of-way to nearby cross traffic, stopping if safety requires it.

questions.q: You drive past a yield sign without stopping and collide with a car in the intersection. How does Texas law view the crash?
options: As prima facie evidence that you failed to yield
As the other driver's fault by default
As no evidence of fault either way
questions.explain: If you pass a yield sign without stopping and then hit a vehicle in the intersection, the collision is prima facie evidence that you did not yield.

questions.q: You have stopped at a stop sign. A car on the cross street has already entered the intersection. What do you do?
options: Go, because you have already stopped
Flash your lights so it stops
Let that car clear the intersection before you go
questions.explain: After stopping at a stop sign you must still yield to vehicles already in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

questions.q: You are driving on a freeway frontage (access) road near an exit ramp. A car is coming off the freeway onto the frontage road. Who must yield?
options: The car leaving the freeway
You, the driver on the frontage road
Neither; the faster car goes first
questions.explain: Drivers on an access or feeder road must yield to vehicles entering it from the highway or leaving it to enter the highway.

questions.q: You are pulling out of a parking lot driveway onto a public street. Who has the right-of-way?
options: Vehicles already traveling on the street
You, once your turn signal is on
Whoever is larger
questions.explain: A driver entering or crossing a road from a driveway, alley, building, or private road must yield to vehicles approaching on that road.

questions.q: You are driving out of an alley in a business district and a sidewalk crosses the alley exit. What must you do first?
options: Honk and drive across the sidewalk
Stop only after reaching the street
Stop before you reach the sidewalk area
questions.explain: When leaving an alley, driveway, or building in a business or residence district, you must stop before moving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.

questions.q: As you leave a driveway, a pedestrian is walking along the sidewalk that crosses it. What should you do?
options: Ease forward so the pedestrian walks behind you
Stop and let the pedestrian pass
Keep going because the pedestrian must wait
questions.explain: A driver entering or leaving a driveway, alley, or building must stop and yield to a pedestrian on the sidewalk that crosses it.

questions.q: An ambulance with flashing lights and a siren is coming up behind you. What should you do?
options: Pull close to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop immediately in your lane
questions.explain: When an emergency vehicle using its signals approaches, you must yield, move as far right as possible, and stop until it has gone by, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

questions.q: A fire truck with siren and lights approaches while you are about to enter an intersection. Where should you pull over and stop?
options: In the middle of the intersection
Against the left curb, inside the intersection
Near the right curb, clear of the intersection
questions.explain: You must move parallel to and close to the right edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop until the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.q: A police car with flashing lights is stopped on the right shoulder. You are in the right lane of a road with two lanes going your way. What does Texas law require?
options: Keep your lane and speed since the car is on the shoulder
Move out of the lane next to the police car if you can, or slow down
Stop in your lane until the officer leaves
questions.explain: Texas's move-over law requires you to leave the lane closest to the stopped vehicle when there are two or more lanes in your direction, or else slow down.

questions.q: The posted limit is 20 mph and you pass a stopped tow truck using its flashing lights without changing lanes. You must slow to no more than ___ mph.
questions.explain: When the posted limit is below 25 mph, the move-over law requires you to slow to 5 mph or less.

questions.q: Besides police cars and ambulances, which vehicle is covered by Texas's move-over or slow-down law?
options: Any car parked on the shoulder
A stopped tow truck using its warning lights
A city bus picking up riders
questions.explain: The law lists specific vehicles, including a stationary tow truck using authorized lights, TxDOT and utility vehicles with lights, and stationary garbage or recycling trucks.

questions.q: The school bus ahead has stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm out. What must you do?
options: Stop before reaching the bus
Pass slowly on the left
Stop only if you see children
questions.explain: When a school bus is stopped to load or unload students and is showing its visual signals, you must stop before reaching it.

questions.q: On an undivided two-lane road, a school bus coming toward you stops with red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: Keep going, because the bus is on the other side
Slow to 20 mph and pass
Stop, because the rule applies from either direction
questions.explain: The school bus law applies to drivers approaching from either direction unless the road has separate roadways.

questions.q: You are stopped behind a school bus with its red lights flashing. Which of these allows you to move again?
options: No children are visible near the bus
The bus driver signals you to proceed
You have waited for one minute
questions.explain: You may go only when the bus starts moving, the bus driver signals you to proceed, or the flashing signals turn off.

questions.q: You are on a highway whose two directions are separated by a raised concrete median. A school bus stops with flashing red lights on the other roadway. What must you do?
options: You are not required to stop, but stay alert
Stop until the bus moves
Stop only if it is a weekday
questions.explain: On a highway with separate roadways divided by a barrier or similar section, you do not have to stop for a school bus on the other roadway.

questions.q: The two directions of a road are separated only by a center left-turn lane. A school bus stops on the other side with red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: Keep going, because the turn lane divides the road
Move into the turn lane and pass
Stop, because a turn lane does not create separate roadways
questions.explain: Texas law says a road separated only by a left-turn lane does not have separate roadways, so you must stop for the school bus.

questions.q: For a first offense of illegally passing a stopped school bus in Texas, the fine is at least $___.
questions.explain: A first offense is a misdemeanor with a fine of not less than $500 and not more than $1,250.

questions.q: There is no traffic signal, and a pedestrian is crossing in the crosswalk on your half of the road. What must you do?
options: Stop and let the pedestrian cross
Drive around the pedestrian carefully
Honk so the pedestrian hurries
questions.explain: Where no traffic signal is operating, you must stop and yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk on your half of the road or close enough from the other half to be in danger.

questions.q: On a multi-lane road, the car in the lane next to you has stopped at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Pass it carefully at a reduced speed
Change lanes behind it and pass
Do not pass it; a pedestrian may be crossing
questions.explain: Texas law forbids passing a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.

questions.q: A pedestrian signal shows "Walk" for people crossing the street you are about to turn onto. What must you do?
options: Turn first because you have a green light
Stop and yield to the pedestrians
Honk to warn them
questions.explain: When a pedestrian faces a "Walk" signal, drivers must stop and yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.

questions.q: Your light is green and you are turning right, but a pedestrian is lawfully crossing the street you are entering. What should you do?
options: Stop and wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing
Turn because a green light gives you the right-of-way
Swing wide to go around the pedestrian
questions.explain: Even on a green light, you must stop and yield to pedestrians lawfully in the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk.

questions.q: A pedestrian crosses mid-block where there is no crosswalk. Which statement is correct?
options: You may keep going because the pedestrian is breaking the law
The pedestrian always has the right-of-way
The pedestrian should yield, but you must still use due care to avoid hitting them
questions.explain: A pedestrian crossing outside a crosswalk must yield to vehicles, yet every driver must still take care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian.

questions.q: You see a small child standing near the edge of the road ahead. What does Texas law expect from you?
options: Keep your speed because the child is not in your lane
Take extra precaution and sound your horn if needed
Flash your headlights and continue
questions.explain: Drivers must use due care, sound the horn when necessary, and take proper precautions when they see a child or a confused person on the roadway.

questions.q: A person using a white cane is crossing at an intersection ahead of you. What must you do?
options: Take every precaution, including stopping fully if needed
Honk to let them know you are there
Go around them if there is room
questions.explain: Drivers must take necessary precautions for a pedestrian with a white cane or assistance animal and come to a full stop if that is the only way to avoid danger.

questions.q: The gates are down and the lights are flashing at this railroad crossing. When may you drive around the gates?
options: When you cannot see a train
After waiting two minutes
Never while the gates are down, closing, or opening
questions.explain: Driving around, under, or through a railroad crossing gate while it is closed, closing, or opening is an offense in Texas.

questions.q: When a railroad signal warns of a train, you must stop at least ___ feet from the nearest rail.
questions.explain: Texas law requires you to stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail.

questions.q: You must stop at a railroad crossing if an approaching train sounds a signal from about ___ feet away and is an immediate hazard.
questions.explain: A stop is required when a train within roughly 1,500 feet sounds a signal audible from that distance and is an immediate hazard.

questions.q: On a two-way road that is wide enough, where must you normally drive?
options: On the right half of the roadway
In the center of the roadway
On whichever half has less traffic
questions.explain: Texas law requires drivers on a roadway of sufficient width to stay on the right half, with limited exceptions such as passing.

questions.q: You are driving slower than the normal flow of traffic on a multi-lane road. Which lane should you use?
options: The left-hand lane
Any lane, as long as you are under the limit
The right-hand lane
questions.explain: A driver moving slower than normal traffic must use the right-hand lane or stay close to the right edge, except when passing or preparing to turn left.

questions.q: On an undivided two-way road with four or more lanes, when may you cross to the left of the center line?
options: To pass a slow car
To turn left into or out of a driveway or alley
Whenever the left lanes are empty
questions.explain: On a two-way road with four or more lanes, you may not drive left of center except in limited cases such as turning left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.q: On a narrow two-way road, you meet an oncoming car. How much of the road must you give it?
options: At least half of the main traveled part, or as much as possible
Only the shoulder
None; the driver going uphill must back up
questions.explain: When meeting a vehicle on a road with one lane each way, you must keep right and give it at least half of the main traveled portion, or as much as you can.

questions.q: After passing a car on the left, when may you move back into the right lane?
options: As soon as your front bumper is past its front bumper
Immediately after you pass its rear bumper
Once you are safely clear of the car you passed
questions.explain: A passing driver must pass at a safe distance and may not return to the right until safely clear of the passed vehicle.

questions.q: Another vehicle is passing you on the left. What must you do?
options: Speed up so it can pass faster
Stay right and do not speed up until it has passed
Move left to block it
questions.explain: A driver being passed must move or stay to the right when signaled and must not accelerate until the passing vehicle is completely by.

questions.q: When you pass using a lane meant for oncoming traffic, you must return to your lane before coming within ___ feet of an approaching vehicle.
questions.explain: Texas law requires you to get back to an authorized lane before you come within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.q: You see these center lines on a two-lane road. What do they mean for passing?
options: Passing allowed in both directions
Passing allowed only for you
No passing for traffic in either direction
questions.explain: Two solid yellow center lines mark a two-direction no-passing zone, and Texas law forbids driving left of no-passing striping.

questions.q: The center line has a solid yellow line on your side and a broken yellow line on the other side. May you pass?
options: Yes, if the road ahead is clear
No, passing is prohibited for you
Yes, but only during daylight
questions.explain: With a solid yellow line next to your lane, crossing to pass is prohibited for you, though drivers on the broken-line side may pass with care.

questions.q: The center line has a broken yellow line on your side and a solid yellow line on the other side. What may you do?
options: Pass when it is safe to do so
Never pass here
Pass only if the other driver signals you
questions.explain: A broken yellow line on your side means you may cross it to pass when the way is clear and passing is safe.

questions.q: What does a single broken yellow center line mean?
options: One-way road with two lanes
No passing in either direction
Two-way road where passing with care is allowed in both directions
questions.explain: A single broken yellow center line separates opposing traffic and allows careful passing for drivers in either direction.

questions.q: Can you cross these lines to turn left into a driveway?
options: No, never under any circumstances
Yes, crossing to turn left into a driveway is allowed when safe
Only if a police officer waves you through
questions.explain: The no-passing rule does not stop you from crossing no-passing striping to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.q: In a city, you may not drive on the left side of the roadway when within ___ feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.explain: Texas law bars driving left of center within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing in a municipality, and also within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.

questions.q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right?
options: Whenever the right shoulder is paved
Any time the driver ahead is going under the limit
When it is turning left and there is room for two lanes going your way
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed only when safe, the vehicle ahead is turning or about to turn left, and the road has enough clear width for two or more lanes in your direction.

questions.q: May you leave the main traveled part of the road to pass a car on the right?
options: Yes, whenever traffic is slow
Only in the specific shoulder cases the law allows
Yes, if you use your turn signal
questions.explain: Passing on the right by leaving the main traveled portion is prohibited except as permitted by the improved-shoulder rules.

questions.q: Which is an allowed reason to drive on the paved right shoulder?
options: To slow down before making a right turn
To get ahead in heavy traffic
To drive faster than the traffic lanes
questions.explain: You may use an improved right shoulder, when necessary and safe, for listed reasons such as slowing before a right turn.

questions.q: A car ahead of you is stopped, waiting to turn left. May you use the paved right shoulder to go around it?
options: No, you must always wait behind it
Yes, at any speed
Yes, if it is necessary and can be done safely
questions.explain: Passing a vehicle that is preparing to turn left is one of the listed reasons you may use an improved right shoulder, if necessary and safe.

questions.q: A faster vehicle wants to pass you on a two-lane highway. What may you do with the paved right shoulder?
options: Nothing; using the shoulder is never allowed
Move onto it briefly to let the faster vehicle pass, if safe
Stay on it for the rest of your trip
questions.explain: Texas law allows driving on an improved right shoulder, when necessary and safe, to let a faster vehicle pass.

questions.q: On a divided highway, when may you use the left (median-side) shoulder?
options: When your vehicle is disabled and you cannot safely reach the right shoulder
Whenever the left lane is backed up
To pass slow traffic
questions.explain: The left shoulder of a divided or controlled-access highway may be used only for a disabled vehicle that cannot safely reach the right shoulder, when a traffic device allows it, or to avoid a collision.

questions.q: On this divided road, what does the solid yellow line on the left side of your lanes mark?
options: A lane you may cross to pass
A bicycle lane
The left edge of the roadway
questions.explain: On divided highways and one-way roads, a solid yellow line marks the left-hand edge of the roadway, while white marks the right edge.

questions.q: You are entering this roundabout. Which way do you travel around the central island?
options: Keep the island on your right
Keep the island on your left, traveling to the right of it
Whichever way is shorter to your exit
questions.explain: Texas law requires drivers moving around a rotary traffic island to drive only to the right of the island.

questions.q: On a road with clearly marked lanes, what must you do?
options: Stay within a single lane and change lanes only when it is safe
Straddle lanes so others can see you
Change lanes freely without checking
questions.explain: On a roadway with two or more marked lanes, you must drive as nearly as practical entirely within one lane and leave it only when safe.

questions.q: What is this center lane, marked with solid and broken yellow lines and opposing arrows, used for?
options: Passing slow vehicles over long distances
Parking during rush hour
Making left turns by traffic from either direction
questions.explain: A center lane bordered by solid and broken yellow lines is a two-way left-turn lane that drivers in either direction use for left turns.

questions.q: Two lanes going the same direction are separated by a broken white line. What does it mean?
options: Lane changes are prohibited
You may change lanes when it is safe
Traffic in the other lane goes the opposite way
questions.explain: A broken white lane line separates traffic moving the same way and allows lane changes with care.

questions.q: What does a solid white line between two lanes going the same direction tell you?
options: Changing lanes here is discouraged
The lanes carry opposite traffic
You must change lanes now
questions.explain: A solid white lane line is used where crossing is discouraged, such as near intersections between a through lane and a turn lane.

questions.q: On a one-way road with three lanes, you move from the right lane into the center lane while a driver in the left lane moves into the center lane too. Who must yield?
options: The driver coming from the left
Whoever signaled last
You, the driver coming from the right
questions.explain: On a one-way road with three or more lanes, a driver entering a lane from the right must yield to a driver entering the same lane from the left.

questions.q: A Texas highway restricts trucks to certain lanes. May a restricted truck use another lane?
options: No, never
Yes, to pass another vehicle or to enter and exit the highway
Only at night
questions.explain: A lane restriction by vehicle class must still let a restricted vehicle use any lane to pass and to enter or leave the highway.

questions.q: How should you make a right turn at an intersection?
options: Approach and turn as close as practical to the right curb or edge
Swing wide into the left lane first
Turn from the center of the road
questions.explain: Both the approach and the right turn itself must be made as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway.

questions.q: Which lane should you be in before turning left at an intersection?
options: The right lane
Any lane, if you signal
The far-left lane lawfully available for your direction
questions.explain: To turn left you must approach in the extreme left lane lawfully available and finish in a lane lawfully available for traffic on the new road.

questions.q: You may not turn around (U-turn) near a curve or hilltop if other drivers cannot see your vehicle from within ___ feet.
questions.explain: Turning to go the opposite direction near a curve or crest of a grade is prohibited if your vehicle is not visible to approaching drivers within 500 feet.

questions.q: Before turning, you must signal continuously for at least the last ___ feet.
questions.explain: Texas law requires a continuous turn signal for not less than the last 100 feet before you turn.

questions.q: When does Texas law require you to use your signal?
options: Only when other cars are nearby
Only for turns at intersections
To turn, change lanes, or pull away from a parked position
questions.explain: You must signal your intent to turn, change lanes, or start from a parked position.

questions.q: A driver behind you wants to pass. May you flash your turn signal to tell them it is safe to pass?
options: Yes, it is the right way to help
No, turn signals may not be used as a courtesy "go ahead" signal
Yes, but only on the right side
questions.explain: Texas law forbids using turn signals as a courtesy or "do pass" signal to a driver approaching from behind.

questions.q: A driver extends the left hand and arm upward out the window. What does this signal mean?
options: Right turn
Left turn
Slowing or stopping
questions.explain: In Texas, a hand and arm extended upward means a right turn; straight out means left, and downward means stop or slow.

questions.q: What does the white diamond symbol in this left lane mean?
options: The lane is ending ahead
It marks a bicycle lane
It is a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) or other preferential lane
questions.explain: A white diamond symbol marks an HOV lane, a preferential lane limited to qualifying vehicles shown on the posted signs.

questions.q: In Texas, you may not stand or park a vehicle within ___ feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.explain: Texas law keeps parked and standing vehicles at least 15 feet away from a fire hydrant so firefighters can reach it.

questions.q: You may not stand or park within ___ feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
questions.explain: Parking must stay at least 20 feet back from a crosswalk at an intersection so drivers and pedestrians can see each other.

questions.q: On the approach to a stop sign at the side of the road, you may not stand or park within ___ feet of the sign.
questions.explain: Texas bars standing or parking within 30 feet on the approach to a stop sign, yield sign, flashing signal or traffic signal at the roadside, so the sign or signal stays visible.

questions.q: You may not park within ___ feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
questions.explain: Parked vehicles must stay at least 50 feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

questions.q: On the same side of the street, you may not stand or park within ___ feet of the driveway entrance to a fire station.
questions.explain: Texas keeps the area within 20 feet of a fire station driveway clear so fire trucks can get out quickly.

questions.q: If a fire station entrance is marked with a sign, you may not park on the opposite side of the street within ___ feet of the entrance.
questions.explain: When the entrance is properly signed, parking across the street within 75 feet of it is not allowed, so fire trucks have room to swing out.

questions.q: When parking on a two-way street, your right-hand wheels must be parallel to and within ___ inches of the right curb or edge of the road.
questions.explain: Texas law requires parallel parking with the right wheels no more than 18 inches from the right curb or road edge.

questions.q: If you must stop on the main traveled part of a highway outside a business or residence district, your vehicle must be in clear view for at least ___ feet in each direction.
questions.explain: A vehicle stopped on the main part of a rural highway must be clearly visible for at least 200 feet each way, and other traffic must still have room to pass.

questions.q: A first offense for parking illegally in a space reserved for people with disabilities carries a fine of at least $___.
questions.explain: A first offense for illegally parking in a disabled space is a misdemeanor with a fine of $500 to $750.

questions.q: A car is already parked at the curb. Can you stop next to it on the traffic side (double-park) for a short time?
options: Yes, if you keep your hazard lights on
No, stopping on the roadway side of a car parked at the curb is not allowed
Yes, for up to five minutes
questions.explain: Texas law bars stopping, standing or parking on the roadway side of a vehicle that is stopped or parked at the curb, because double parking blocks a traffic lane.

questions.q: Unless traffic or an officer requires it, in which place may you NOT stop your vehicle at all?
options: On the shoulder of a rural road, well clear of traffic
In a marked parking space on a city street
On a bridge or in a highway tunnel
questions.explain: Stopping, standing and parking are all banned on a bridge or other elevated highway structure and in a highway tunnel.

questions.q: Which of these places is always off-limits for stopping, standing or parking under Texas law?
options: On a railroad track
Next to an unmarked curb on a residential street
In a parking lot space
questions.explain: You may never stop, stand or park on a railroad track; a train cannot stop quickly to avoid you.

questions.q: When may you stand a vehicle in front of someone's private driveway?
options: Any time, if you stay in the car
Only for a moment to pick up or drop off a passenger
Never, not even to let a passenger out
questions.explain: Standing or parking in front of a public or private driveway is banned, except for a brief stop to pick up or let out a passenger.

questions.q: You need to stop within 50 feet of the nearest rail at a crossing marked by this sign. When is that allowed?
options: Only while temporarily loading or unloading merchandise or passengers
Whenever no train is in sight
Never, under any circumstances
questions.explain: The 50-foot no-parking rule at railroad crossings has a narrow exception for temporarily loading or unloading goods or passengers.

questions.q: On a two-way street, how must you parallel park?
options: Facing either direction, as long as you are close to the curb
With your left wheels next to the left curb
With your right wheels next to the right curb, facing the direction of traffic
questions.explain: On a two-way roadway you park on the right, parallel to the right curb or edge with your right-hand wheels close to it, so you face the same way as traffic in that lane.

questions.q: On a one-way street with no local rule saying otherwise, where may you parallel park?
options: Only along the right curb
Along the right curb or the left curb, facing the direction of traffic
Along either curb, facing either direction
questions.explain: On a one-way roadway you may park with your right wheels within 18 inches of the right curb or your left wheels within 18 inches of the left curb, pointed the way traffic moves.

questions.q: Outside a business or residence district, when may you stop on the main traveled part of a highway?
options: Only if pulling off the road is not practical, other traffic can still pass, and your vehicle can be seen from far enough away
Any time your hazard lights are on
Whenever you need to check a map or make a phone call
questions.explain: On rural highways you must pull off the main traveled lanes if you can; stopping on them is allowed only when leaving the road is not practical, a lane stays open beside you, and you are clearly visible.

questions.q: This sign stands at the side of the road ahead. How close to it may you park on your approach?
options: No closer than 15 feet
No closer than 30 feet
Right up to the sign
questions.explain: Texas bars standing or parking within 30 feet on the approach to a yield sign, stop sign or roadside signal, so other drivers can see it.

questions.q: You are leaving your car parked on a downhill street next to a curb. Why are the front wheels turned as shown?
options: It makes the car easier to pull out later
It is only needed for trucks
Texas law requires turning the front wheels to the curb when an unattended car is on a grade
questions.explain: When you leave a vehicle unattended on a grade, Texas law requires turning the front wheels to the curb or side of the road so the car will not roll into traffic.

questions.q: Before walking away from your parked car, what does Texas law require you to do?
options: Turn on the hazard lights and leave the engine idling
Stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key and set the parking brake
Leave the key in the car so it can be moved if needed
questions.explain: An unattended vehicle must have the engine off, the ignition locked, the key removed and the parking brake set.

questions.q: May you leave your car unattended with the engine running after starting it with a remote starter?
options: Yes, if the car cannot be driven until the key is in the ignition or inside the car
No, the engine must always be off when the car is unattended
Yes, but only for up to 30 minutes
questions.explain: The engine-off, locked-ignition and key-removal rules do not apply to a remote start when the car cannot be driven unless the key is in the ignition or physically inside the car.

questions.q: You are parked at the curb and ready to leave. When may you pull out?
options: As soon as your turn signal has been on for a few seconds
Only when you can move out safely
Whenever the car behind you flashes its lights
questions.explain: A stopped or parked vehicle may start moving only when the movement can be made safely; signaling alone does not give you the right to pull out.

questions.q: You are parked on a busy street. What is the rule for opening the door on the traffic side?
options: Open it whenever you like; passing drivers must avoid you
Never open a traffic-side door on a public street
Open it only when it is reasonably safe and close it as soon as you finish loading or unloading
questions.explain: You may open a door on the traffic side only if you can do so safely without interfering with traffic, and you may not leave it open longer than needed to load or unload a passenger.

questions.q: In Texas, a disabled parking placard issued for a TEMPORARY disability shows the access symbol on a shield of which color?
questions.explain: Texas placards show the white access symbol on a red shield for a temporary disability and on a blue shield for a permanent disability.

questions.q: Where should a disabled parking placard be placed when you use a disabled parking space?
options: On the rearview mirror
On the rear bumper
Kept in the glove compartment, to show if asked
questions.explain: Parking privileges apply when the placard is hung on the rearview mirror at the front windshield, or when the vehicle has disabled license plates.

questions.q: You park in a regular space but your car sticks into the striped access aisle beside a disabled space. Is this a violation?
options: No, only parking inside the disabled space itself is an offense
Yes, blocking an access aisle or curb ramp is an offense
Only if a person with a disability complains
questions.explain: Texas makes it an offense to leave a vehicle where it blocks an access aisle, curb ramp or other feature built to help people with disabilities.

questions.q: A driver displaying a valid disabled parking placard wants to park in a fire lane where signs prohibit parking. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, a placard allows parking anywhere
Yes, for up to one hour
No, a placard does not allow parking where parking is prohibited
questions.explain: Disabled parking privileges do not let a vehicle park at a time or place where parking is prohibited.

questions.q: Your relative lends you their disabled parking placard, and you use it to park in a disabled space while running your own errands. Who has broken the law?
options: Only the relative, because it is their placard
Both of you: illegal use of the space is an offense, and so is lending a placard that gets misused
Nobody, because the placard is valid
questions.explain: Using a disabled space without being or transporting the placard holder is an offense, and lending your placard to someone who misuses it is a separate offense.

questions.q: Can you park your car with two wheels on the sidewalk to leave more room in the street?
options: No, stopping, standing or parking a motor vehicle on a sidewalk is not allowed
Yes, if the street is narrow
Yes, at night only
questions.explain: Texas law bars stopping, standing or parking a vehicle on a sidewalk; only bicycles may be parked there, and only if they do not block pedestrians.

questions.q: Unless traffic or an officer requires it, where is stopping your vehicle prohibited?
options: In a marked loading zone while unloading
In an intersection or on a crosswalk
In a driveway on your own property
questions.explain: You may not stop, stand or park in an intersection or on a crosswalk unless you must do so to avoid traffic or to obey an officer or traffic control device.

questions.q: Under Texas law, a person with an alcohol concentration of ___ or more is legally intoxicated.
questions.explain: Texas defines intoxicated as including an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

questions.q: An adult driver's breath test shows 0.06. Can the driver still be considered intoxicated in Texas?
options: No, a result under 0.08 means the driver is legally sober
Only if the driver is carrying an open container
Yes, if alcohol has taken away the normal use of the driver's mental or physical faculties
questions.explain: Texas has two ways to be intoxicated: a 0.08 or higher alcohol concentration, or losing the normal use of your mental or physical abilities because of alcohol or another substance.

questions.q: Which of the following can make a driver legally intoxicated in Texas?
options: Alcohol, drugs, or any other substance that takes away the normal use of the driver's faculties
Only alcohol
Only illegal drugs
questions.explain: Texas counts impairment caused by alcohol, controlled substances, drugs, dangerous drugs, combinations of them, or any other substance.

questions.q: A driver is impaired by a medicine their doctor prescribed. In a Texas DWI case, does the prescription excuse them?
options: Yes, a valid prescription is a complete defense
No, being entitled to use the drug is not a defense
Yes, if the driver was below 0.08
questions.explain: Texas law says it is not a defense that the driver was legally entitled to use the substance that impaired them.

questions.q: In Texas, the offense of driving while intoxicated (DWI) is committed when a person is intoxicated while:
options: Operating a motor vehicle in a public place
Operating a motor vehicle on an interstate highway only
Sitting in a parked car with the engine off on private land
questions.explain: DWI means being intoxicated while operating a motor vehicle in a public place, not just on highways.

questions.q: A basic first-offense DWI in Texas carries a minimum jail term of ___ hours.
questions.explain: A standard DWI is a Class B misdemeanor with at least 72 hours of confinement.

questions.q: If a DWI driver had an open container of alcohol within reach, the minimum jail term rises to ___ days.
questions.explain: Having an open container in the driver's immediate possession raises the DWI minimum confinement to six days.

questions.q: A DWI becomes a Class A misdemeanor if a blood, breath or urine test shows an alcohol concentration of ___ or more.
questions.explain: A test result of 0.15 or higher raises a DWI from a Class B to a Class A misdemeanor.

questions.q: What happens to a DWI charge if the driver was in a school crossing zone while its reduced speed limit was in effect?
options: It stays a Class B misdemeanor
It becomes a state jail felony
It is handled only as a speeding ticket
questions.explain: Driving while intoxicated in an active school crossing zone turns DWI into a state jail felony.

questions.q: Driving while intoxicated with a passenger younger than ___ years old is a state jail felony in Texas.
questions.explain: DWI with a passenger under 15 is a separate offense, DWI with child passenger, and it is a state jail felony.

questions.q: A DWI driver with one prior intoxication conviction faces a Class A misdemeanor with at least ___ days in jail.
questions.explain: With one prior conviction for an intoxication offense, DWI becomes a Class A misdemeanor with a minimum of 30 days of confinement.

questions.q: A driver with two prior DWI convictions is convicted of DWI again. What level of offense is it?
options: A felony of the third degree
A Class B misdemeanor
A Class C misdemeanor
questions.explain: DWI after two prior convictions for intoxication offenses such as DWI is a third-degree felony.

questions.q: An intoxicated driver causes a crash that leaves another person with a serious bodily injury. What offense is this?
options: Reckless driving, a misdemeanor
Intoxication assault, a felony
Open container, a Class C misdemeanor
questions.explain: Causing serious bodily injury to someone because of intoxication while driving is intoxication assault, normally a third-degree felony.

questions.q: An intoxicated driver causes a crash in which someone dies. In Texas this is intoxication manslaughter, which is normally a:
options: Class A misdemeanor
State jail felony
Second-degree felony
questions.explain: Causing a death by accident or mistake because of intoxication while driving is intoxication manslaughter, a second-degree felony unless enhanced.

questions.q: Under the Texas open container law, which of these counts as an open container?
options: Only a container that is more than half full
Any container of alcohol that has been opened, has a broken seal, or has had some contents removed
Only a container held in the driver's hand
questions.explain: An open container is any bottle, can or other receptacle holding any amount of alcohol that is open, has been opened, has a broken seal, or is partly emptied.

questions.q: You are driving home with a partly finished bottle of wine. Where can you legally carry it in a car that has a trunk?
options: In the trunk
On the back seat, if the cork is pushed back in
In an unlocked center console
questions.explain: The open container law covers the passenger area; the trunk and a locked glove compartment are not part of the passenger area.

questions.q: Your car is parked on the shoulder of a public road and you have an open can of beer in the front seat. Does the open container law apply?
options: No, it applies only while the car is moving
No, it applies only to the driver
Yes, it applies whether the car is moving, stopped or parked on a public highway
questions.explain: Knowingly having an open container in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public highway is an offense even if the vehicle is stopped or parked.

questions.q: In which situation is a passenger NOT violating the open container law?
options: Riding in the back seat of a friend's car
Riding as a passenger in a limousine or taxi that carries people for pay
Riding in the front seat of a pickup truck
questions.explain: The law makes an exception for passengers in vehicles used mainly to carry people for pay, such as buses, taxis and limousines, and for the living quarters of motor homes.

questions.q: By itself, having an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a vehicle is what level of offense in Texas?
options: Class C misdemeanor
Class A misdemeanor
Felony
questions.explain: The open container offense is a Class C misdemeanor, and the officer normally issues a citation instead of taking the person to a magistrate.

questions.q: Under the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code, a "minor" is anyone under ___ years of age.
questions.explain: For alcohol laws, Texas defines a minor as a person under 21.

questions.q: How much alcohol may a driver under 21 have in their system while driving in a public place in Texas?
options: Up to 0.02
Up to 0.08, the same as adults
None; any detectable amount is an offense
questions.explain: A minor commits an offense by driving in a public place with any detectable amount of alcohol in their system.

questions.q: A 19-year-old drinks one beer, feels fine, and drives home. A test shows a small but detectable amount of alcohol. What is the result?
options: The driver has committed the offense of driving under the influence by a minor
No offense, because the driver was not impaired
No offense, because the level was below 0.08
questions.explain: For drivers under 21 the law does not require impairment; any detectable alcohol while driving in a public place is an offense.

questions.q: A minor convicted of driving under the influence for the first time must perform at least ___ hours of alcohol-related community service.
questions.explain: A first conviction requires 20 to 40 hours of community service tied to alcohol education or prevention, in addition to any fine.

questions.q: Under Texas law, when may a person under 21 legally have an alcoholic beverage in their possession?
options: Whenever they are at a private party
When they are in the visible presence of their adult parent, guardian or spouse
Whenever the container is still sealed
questions.explain: Possession by a minor is an offense, with limited exceptions such as being in the visible presence of an adult parent, guardian or spouse, or while working for a licensed seller.

questions.q: What does Texas's implied consent law mean for a driver arrested for DWI?
options: The driver must take a field sobriety test before any arrest
The driver may choose to give a urine sample instead of any other test
By driving, the driver is considered to have agreed to give breath or blood specimens for testing
questions.explain: A person arrested for an intoxication offense while driving in a public place is deemed to have consented to give breath or blood specimens for alcohol or drug testing.

questions.q: Does Texas's implied consent law apply to a driver under 21 arrested for driving with any detectable alcohol?
options: Yes, it covers that offense too
No, it applies only to drivers 21 and older
Only if the minor's parent agrees
questions.explain: Implied consent covers arrests for the minor driving-under-the-influence offense as well as for driving while intoxicated.

questions.q: If you refuse an officer's request for a breath or blood specimen and have no alcohol- or drug-related enforcement contact in the previous 10 years, your license will be suspended for ___ days.
questions.explain: Refusing a requested specimen leads to a 180-day license suspension when your record has no alcohol- or drug-related enforcement contact in the previous 10 years.

questions.q: A driver refuses a breath test, and their record shows an alcohol-related enforcement contact within the last 10 years. How long is the suspension?
options: 180 days
90 days
Two years
questions.explain: The refusal suspension grows from 180 days to two years if the driver's record shows an alcohol- or drug-related enforcement contact in the previous 10 years.

questions.q: An adult with no alcohol- or drug-related enforcement contacts in the past 10 years who takes the test and is at or above the legal limit faces an automatic license suspension of ___ days.
questions.explain: For an adult with no alcohol- or drug-related enforcement contact in the past 10 years, failing the test brings a 90-day administrative suspension, whether or not there is a criminal case.

questions.q: A driver under 21 with no prior alcohol-driving convictions who is found driving with any detectable alcohol faces an automatic license suspension of ___ days.
questions.explain: The administrative suspension for a minor with no prior alcohol-driving convictions is 60 days; it rises to 120 and then 180 days with prior convictions.

questions.q: After receiving a notice of suspension for refusing or failing an alcohol test, you have ___ days to request a hearing.
questions.explain: You have a right to a hearing if the department receives your written request no later than the 15th day after you receive the notice of suspension.

questions.q: When does a license suspension for refusing a breath or blood test normally take effect?
options: Immediately at the time of arrest
On the 40th day after the driver receives the notice of suspension
Only after the driver is convicted of DWI
questions.explain: A refusal suspension begins on the 40th day after the driver receives, or is considered to have received, the notice, and it does not depend on a criminal conviction.

questions.q: Before asking for a specimen, a Texas officer must warn you about the consequences of refusing. Which is one of them?
options: The refusal may be used as evidence against you, and the officer may seek a warrant to take a specimen
Refusing ends the investigation and you are free to drive away
Refusing gives you a lighter penalty if you are later convicted
questions.explain: The officer must tell you that a refusal may be admissible in court, your license will be suspended, and the officer may apply for a warrant to take a specimen anyway.

questions.q: A court orders an ignition interlock device on a DWI offender's car. What does the device do?
options: It limits the car's top speed
It records the driver's location for the court
It tests the driver's breath and makes the car impractical to operate if alcohol is detected
questions.explain: An ignition interlock uses a deep-lung breath test to keep the vehicle from being operated if alcohol is found in the driver's breath.

questions.q: A driver convicted of DWI and placed on community supervision had a test result of 0.15 or higher. What must the court require?
options: Nothing beyond a fine
An ignition interlock device on the vehicle the person owns or most often drives
Only a defensive driving course
questions.explain: When a DWI test showed 0.15 or more, the court must order an ignition interlock as a condition of community supervision, and the person may drive only vehicles that have one.

questions.q: How much space does Texas law require you to keep behind the vehicle you are following?
options: Enough to stop safely without hitting it or swerving into something else, given your speed and conditions
At least 100 feet at all times
Exactly one car length for every 10 mph, no matter the conditions
questions.explain: Texas uses an 'assured clear distance' rule: the gap must let you stop safely for the speed, traffic and road conditions, rather than a fixed number.

questions.q: Outside a business or residential district, a truck following another truck should, when conditions allow, leave a gap large enough for what?
options: A passing vehicle to safely move into the space
The trucks to be linked by a tow chain
A pedestrian to cross between them
questions.explain: Texas asks trucks traveling behind each other on open roads to leave enough room for a passing vehicle to pull into the gap.

questions.q: Besides nighttime, when must you turn on your headlights in Texas?
options: Only on highways with a speed limit above 55 mph
Only when it is actually raining
Whenever people or vehicles on the highway cannot be clearly seen 1,000 feet ahead
questions.explain: Lights are required at night and any time poor light or weather keeps you from clearly seeing persons or vehicles 1,000 feet ahead.

questions.q: Texas law requires your lights to be on when a person or vehicle on the highway is not clearly visible at a distance of ___ feet ahead.
questions.explain: The visibility trigger for using lights is 1,000 feet.

questions.q: Under Texas law, 'nighttime' (when headlights are required) begins when?
options: One hour after sunset
At sunset exactly
One-half hour after sunset
questions.explain: Texas defines nighttime as the period from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise.

questions.q: When an oncoming vehicle comes within ___ feet, you must switch from high beams to low beams.
