questions.explain: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle you must use your lower beam or a beam aimed so it does not shine into the other driver's eyes.

questions.q: When you are coming up behind another vehicle, you may not use your high beams within ___ feet of it.
questions.explain: Texas bars the upper beam when you are within 300 feet of a vehicle you are approaching from behind.

questions.q: You are driving at night with high beams on and a car appears ahead going the same direction, about 200 feet away. What should you do?
options: Switch to low beams
Flash your high beams to warn the driver
Keep high beams on so the other driver sees you
questions.explain: High beams are not allowed within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following, so you must dim them.

questions.q: Who is legally responsible for buckling up a 16-year-old passenger in Texas?
options: The driver, because the passenger is under 17
Only the passenger
Nobody, seat belts are optional for passengers
questions.explain: A driver commits an offense by letting a child younger than 17 ride without a seat belt (unless a child safety seat is required instead).

questions.q: A 30-year-old passenger in your car is not wearing a seat belt. Under Texas law, who commits the offense?
options: Neither person, since passengers are exempt
Only the driver
The passenger, because riders 15 and older are responsible for their own belt
questions.explain: Anyone at least 15 years old riding in a seat that has a belt must wear it, and that person is the one who violates the law.

questions.q: Texas requires a child to ride in a child safety seat system if the child is younger than ___ years old, unless the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches.
questions.explain: Children under 8 must be in a child passenger safety seat system unless they are taller than 4 feet 9 inches.

questions.q: A 7-year-old who is shorter than 4 feet 9 inches rides in your car. What does Texas law require?
options: Secure the child in a child safety seat system following the manufacturer's instructions
The child may ride unbelted in the back seat
An adult lap belt is enough
questions.explain: A child under 8 who is not taller than 4 feet 9 inches must be kept in a child safety seat system used the way the maker instructs.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child is 4 feet 10 inches tall. Does Texas law require a child safety seat?
options: No, and the child does not need any restraint
Yes, every child under 8 needs a safety seat regardless of height
No, because the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches; the child still must wear a seat belt
questions.explain: The safety-seat rule does not apply to a child taller than 4 feet 9 inches, but the driver must still make sure a child under 17 is belted.

questions.q: Under Texas law, when may a driver read, write or send a text message on a handheld phone?
options: Only when the vehicle is stopped
Whenever the phone is held at eye level
Whenever traffic is moving under 30 mph
questions.explain: Texas bans using a portable device to read, write or send electronic messages while driving unless the vehicle is stopped.

questions.q: Which phone use is a defense under the Texas texting-while-driving law?
options: Replying to a friend's text at a red light while rolling forward
Reading a social media post
Using the phone to navigate with GPS
questions.explain: Navigation with a GPS or navigation system is one of the listed defenses; reading or sending non-emergency messages while moving is not.

questions.q: You are driving through a marked school crossing zone. When may you use your cell phone?
options: Only to send short text messages
Any time, if you hold the phone below the window
Only if the vehicle is stopped or you use a hands-free device
questions.explain: In a school crossing zone a driver may not use a wireless device unless stopped or using it hands-free (emergency calls are a defense).

questions.q: On public school property where a school crossing zone has its reduced speed limit in effect, how may a driver use a cell phone?
options: Only while stopped or with a hands-free device
Freely, because the ban applies only on public streets
Only to send text messages
questions.explain: Texas extends the school-zone phone limits to school property while the reduced school-zone speed is in effect.

questions.q: You are in a collision that injures someone, and you have already driven a short distance away. What must you do?
options: Wait until the next day and file a report by mail
Call your insurer and keep driving
Return to the scene immediately
questions.explain: A driver in an injury or death crash must stop at the scene, or return to it right away if not already stopped there.

questions.q: After a crash that may have hurt someone, what must the driver find out right away?
options: Whether anyone was involved and needs help
Whether the damage is over $1,000
Who was at fault
questions.explain: Drivers must immediately determine whether a person is involved and, if so, whether that person needs aid.

questions.q: When you stop after a collision, how should you position your vehicle?
options: At or as close as possible to the scene, without blocking traffic more than necessary
At the nearest gas station, wherever it is
In the exact spot of impact even if it blocks every lane
questions.explain: Texas requires stopping at or near the scene while avoiding more traffic obstruction than needed.

questions.q: You have a minor crash on a freeway in a metropolitan area and both cars can be driven normally. What should you do?
options: Drive home and exchange information later by phone
Leave the cars in the lane until police arrive
Move the cars off the main lanes to a safe nearby spot, such as the frontage road, to exchange information
questions.explain: If every vehicle can be driven safely, drivers must move to a designated site, frontage road, cross street or other suitable place to finish their duties.

questions.q: Which information must you give the other driver after a crash in Texas?
options: Your date of birth and employer
Your name, address, vehicle registration number and liability insurer
Only your phone number
questions.explain: Drivers must share their name, address, the vehicle's registration number and the name of their liability insurance company.

questions.q: After a collision, another involved driver asks to see your driver license. What does Texas law require?
options: Refuse, since only police may ask
Hand it over for them to keep
Show it if you have it with you
questions.explain: If requested and available, a driver involved in a crash must show their license to the other people involved.

questions.q: A person hurt in a crash with you clearly needs medical treatment. What must you do?
options: Move the person into your car only if police tell you to
Give reasonable help, including taking or arranging transport to a doctor or hospital
Leave, because only emergency workers may help
questions.explain: Drivers must provide reasonable assistance to injured people, including arranging transportation for medical care when it is clearly needed or requested.

questions.q: You back into a parked car and nobody is around. What does Texas law require?
options: Stop, then find the owner or leave a written note with your name, address and what happened
Wait 10 minutes, then leave if no one returns
Drive away if the damage looks minor
questions.explain: When you damage an unattended vehicle, you must stop and either locate the owner or securely leave a visible written notice with your information and the circumstances.

questions.q: You hit a fence next to the highway, and only the fence is damaged. What must you do?
options: Nothing, because no vehicle was damaged
Repair the fence yourself before telling anyone
Take reasonable steps to find and notify the property owner
questions.explain: Damaging a structure, fixture or landscaping next to a highway requires reasonable steps to locate the owner and give your name, address and registration number.

questions.q: A crash inside city limits leaves a car unable to be driven safely. Whom must you notify right away?
options: The local police department
The Texas Department of Insurance
Your vehicle's manufacturer
questions.explain: Crashes causing injury, death or a vehicle that cannot be driven normally must be reported immediately; inside a city, that means the local police.

questions.q: Which collision must be reported immediately to police or the sheriff by the quickest means?
options: Only collisions involving commercial trucks
One that injures a person or leaves a vehicle unable to be driven safely
Any collision, even a light scrape in a parking lot
questions.explain: Immediate notice is required when a crash causes injury or death or damages a vehicle so it cannot be driven normally and safely.

questions.q: Under Texas law, may a 12-year-old ride in the open bed of your pickup on a city street?
options: Yes, if the tailgate is closed
No, it is an offense to drive with a child under 18 in an open truck bed, except in limited situations
Yes, as long as you drive under 35 mph
questions.explain: Texas makes it an offense to drive an open-bed pickup with a child younger than 18 in the bed, apart from narrow exceptions such as parades or emergencies.

questions.q: When may you drive a car across a sidewalk in Texas?
options: Only at a permanent or authorized temporary driveway
Whenever no pedestrians are present
To get around traffic that is stopped
questions.explain: Driving on a sidewalk or sidewalk area is prohibited except where a permanent or authorized temporary driveway crosses it.

questions.q: You are parked on a busy street. Before opening your door on the traffic side, what must you do?
options: Open it quickly so traffic notices you
Turn on your hazard lights and open it
Make sure it can be opened safely without interfering with moving traffic
questions.explain: Texas law allows opening a door on the traffic side only when it is reasonably safe and does not interfere with traffic, and it may not be left open longer than needed.

questions.q: You missed your exit on a controlled-access freeway. What may you do?
options: Back up in the right lane with hazard lights on
Back up slowly on the shoulder
Continue to the next exit; backing on the shoulder or roadway is not allowed
questions.explain: Texas prohibits backing on the shoulder or roadway of a limited-access or controlled-access highway.

questions.q: On a Texas roadway, what rights and duties does a person riding a bicycle have?
options: The same as a pedestrian
Generally the same as a driver of a vehicle
None; bicycles must stay on sidewalks
questions.explain: A bicyclist has the rights and duties of a vehicle driver unless a specific rule says otherwise or the rule cannot apply to bicycles.

questions.q: Two bicyclists are riding side by side in a single lane ahead of you and not blocking normal traffic flow. Is this legal in Texas?
options: Yes, bicyclists may ride two abreast in a single lane if they do not impede normal traffic
No, bicyclists must always ride single file
Yes, and they may ride three or more abreast
questions.explain: Texas allows riding two abreast within one lane as long as the riders do not impede the normal flow of traffic.

questions.q: A cyclist is riding near the middle of a narrow outside lane that is under 14 feet wide and has no bike lane. Is that allowed?
options: No, cyclists must always hug the right curb
No, cyclists may not use lanes without a bike lane
Yes, a cyclist may move away from the right edge when the lane is too narrow to share safely
questions.explain: The keep-right rule for slower bicycles has exceptions, including an outside lane less than 14 feet wide without a bike lane or too narrow to share side by side.

questions.q: At night in Texas, a bicycle's front lamp must emit white light visible from at least ___ feet ahead.
questions.explain: A bicycle used at night needs a front white lamp visible from at least 500 feet, plus a red rear reflector or lamp.

questions.q: Under Texas law, a motorcycle may not carry a passenger younger than ___ years old, unless the child rides in a sidecar.
questions.explain: A motorcycle or moped operator may not carry a passenger under 5 years old, except a child seated in an attached sidecar.

questions.q: According to NHTSA, sending or reading a text takes your eyes off the road for about 5 seconds. At 55 mph, how far do you travel in that time?
options: About the length of a football field
About a quarter mile
About one car length
questions.explain: NHTSA notes that 5 seconds at 55 mph covers roughly the length of a football field driven blind.

questions.q: NHTSA advises that children of what age should ride in the back seat?
options: Under 18
Under 13
Under 5
questions.explain: Because frontal air bags deploy with great force, NHTSA recommends that children under 13 sit in the back seat.

questions.q: How should a lap-and-shoulder seat belt be worn, according to NHTSA?
options: Lap belt across the stomach and shoulder belt behind the back
Lap belt across the hips and shoulder belt across the middle of the chest
Shoulder belt under the arm for comfort
questions.explain: NHTSA says the lap belt goes across the hips, the shoulder belt across the mid-chest away from the neck, and never behind the back or under an arm.

questions.q: Why do you still need a seat belt in a car with air bags?
options: Air bags only work if you are unbelted
Seat belts are only needed in older cars
Air bags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them
questions.explain: NHTSA explains that air bags supplement seat belts, and an unbelted occupant can be thrown into a deploying air bag and badly hurt.

questions.q: According to NHTSA, when do drowsy-driving crashes most often happen?
options: Between midnight and 6 a.m., or in the late afternoon
Between 8 a.m. and noon
Right after eating breakfast
questions.explain: NHTSA reports that drowsy-driving crashes peak from midnight to 6 a.m. and in the late afternoon, when the body's internal clock dips.

questions.q: You start to feel sleepy while driving. What does NHTSA suggest?
options: Pull over in a safe place, such as a lighted rest stop, for a short nap
Speed up to reach your destination sooner
Open the window and turn up the radio
questions.explain: NHTSA says coffee alone is not enough; pulling over somewhere safe for a short nap helps, though only for a limited time.

questions.q: You are about to turn right across a bike lane while a cyclist rides in it beside you. What should you do?
options: Honk so the cyclist stops
Speed up to turn ahead of the cyclist
Yield and let the cyclist pass before turning
questions.explain: NHTSA advises drivers to yield to bicyclists as they would to other vehicles and to avoid turning in front of them.

questions.q: According to NHTSA, what usually causes multi-vehicle crashes involving motorcycles?
options: The motorcyclist was riding too slowly
The other driver simply did not see the motorcyclist
The motorcycle's brakes failed
questions.explain: NHTSA notes most multi-vehicle motorcycle crashes happen because other drivers did not see the rider, so check carefully for motorcycles.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to get a Texas learner license?
questions.explain: A learner license may be issued to someone who is at least 15 and under 18 and meets the education and testing requirements.

questions.q: A learner license holder must be accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least ___ years old, seated beside the driver.
questions.explain: The supervising driver must sit in the seat next to the learner, be at least 21, hold the right license, and have at least one year of driving experience.

questions.q: Besides age and holding the right license, what driving experience must a learner's supervising driver have?
options: None, any license holder qualifies
At least one year
At least five years
questions.explain: Texas requires the adult beside a learner to have at least one year of driving experience.

questions.q: Where must the supervising adult sit when a learner license holder is driving?
options: In the seat next to the driver
In any back seat
Anywhere in the vehicle
questions.explain: A learner may drive only while accompanied by a qualified licensed adult occupying the seat beside the operator.

questions.q: Which supervising adult is breaking Texas law while a learner drives?
options: One who is asleep in the front passenger seat
One who is watching the road and giving directions
One who is 45 years old with 20 years of driving experience
questions.explain: The person beside a learner commits an offense if they sleep, are intoxicated, or are doing something that keeps them from watching and responding to the driver.

questions.q: When may a learner license holder drive?
options: Alone during daylight hours
Only with the learner license in their possession and a qualified adult beside them
Alone, if a parent gave written permission
questions.explain: A learner license allows driving only while the license is carried and a qualified supervising driver occupies the seat beside the learner.

questions.q: How long must a driver under 18 hold a learner (or hardship) license before getting a provisional Class C license?
options: At least 30 days
At least one year
At least six months
questions.explain: Texas will not issue a regular Class C license to an applicant under 18 who has not held a learner or hardship license for at least six months.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to get a Texas provisional Class C license?
questions.explain: An applicant under 18 must be at least 16, among other requirements, to receive a Class C license.

questions.q: A Texas driver under 18 may not drive with more than ___ passenger(s) under 21 who are not family members.
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 may carry no more than one non-family passenger under 21 (this does not apply while supervised as a learner requires).

questions.q: A 17-year-old provisional driver wants to drive at 1 a.m. to see friends. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, on weekends only
Yes, if the friends are over 21
No; drivers under 18 may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. except for work, school activities or a medical emergency
questions.explain: Texas restricts drivers under 18 from driving between midnight and 5 a.m. unless it is needed for a job, a school-related activity or a medical emergency.

questions.q: Which reason allows a 16-year-old to drive between midnight and 5 a.m. in Texas?
options: Picking up friends from a party
Driving home from a job
Driving to a late movie
questions.explain: The late-night restriction has exceptions only for employment, school-related activities and medical emergencies.

questions.q: May a driver under 18 talk on a phone using a hands-free device while driving in Texas?
options: Yes, hands-free calls are allowed
No, all wireless device use is banned except in an emergency
Yes, but only on highways
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 may not drive while using a wireless communication device, which includes hands-free devices, except in an emergency.

questions.q: When does a Texas provisional license expire?
options: On the holder's 18th birthday
One year after it is issued
On the holder's 21st birthday
questions.explain: Both provisional and learner licenses expire on the holder's 18th birthday.

questions.q: When does a Texas learner license expire?
options: On the holder's 16th birthday
Six months after it is issued
On the holder's 18th birthday
questions.explain: A learner license expires on the 18th birthday of the holder.

questions.q: After moving to a new home address, you must notify the Texas Department of Public Safety within ___ days.
questions.explain: Texas requires you to report an address change no later than the 30th day after the move and apply for a duplicate license.

questions.q: You get married and change your last name. What must you do about your Texas driver license?
options: Nothing until the license expires
Notify your insurance company only
Notify DPS within 30 days and apply for a duplicate license
questions.explain: A name change must be reported within 30 days, along with an application for a duplicate license.

questions.q: What does Texas law require you to do with your driver license while you drive?
options: Carry it with you and show it when a peace officer asks
Keep a photo of it on your phone instead
Leave it at home to prevent loss
questions.explain: Drivers must have the proper class of license in their possession and display it on demand of a peace officer, magistrate or court officer.

questions.q: What is the minimum Texas liability insurance coverage for bodily injury to one person in one crash?
questions.explain: Texas minimum coverage is $30,000 per injured person, $60,000 per crash, and $25,000 for property damage (30/60/25).

questions.q: Texas minimum liability insurance must cover at least $___ for injuries to two or more people in one crash.
questions.explain: The minimum for bodily injury or death of two or more people in one collision is $60,000.

questions.q: What is the minimum Texas liability coverage for damage to other people's property in one crash?
questions.explain: Texas requires at least $25,000 of coverage for damage to or destruction of others' property per collision.

questions.q: A police officer asks for proof of insurance. Which of these is acceptable in Texas?
options: Your vehicle registration sticker
An insurer-provided image of your insurance card on your phone
A verbal statement of your insurer's name
questions.explain: Texas accepts several forms of proof, including the standard insurance card or an image of it from your insurer displayed on a wireless device.

questions.q: What must you have before driving a motor vehicle in Texas, in addition to a license?
options: Financial responsibility, usually a liability insurance policy
A membership in a roadside assistance club
A certificate from a mechanic
questions.explain: A person may not operate a vehicle in Texas unless financial responsibility is established, most commonly through liability insurance.

questions.q: An officer who investigates a crash must write a report if someone is injured or killed, or if one person's property damage appears to be at least ___ dollars.
questions.explain: Texas officers must file a written crash report for injury or death crashes or apparent property damage of $1,000 or more to any one person.

questions.q: Which Texas license class is needed for a single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more?
options: Class M
Class C
Class A or Class B, depending on what it tows
questions.explain: Vehicles rated over 26,000 pounds fall under Class A or Class B, not Class C; Class A also covers heavy combinations towing more than 10,000 pounds.

questions.q: Which license class lets you drive a combination of vehicles rated 26,001 pounds or more when the towed vehicle is rated over 10,000 pounds?
options: Class A
Class C
Class B
questions.explain: Class A covers combinations of 26,001 pounds or more when any towed vehicle is rated over 10,000 pounds.

questions.q: Which Texas license class is required to drive a bus that seats 24 or more passengers, including the driver?
options: Class M
Class B
Class C
questions.explain: A Class B license covers buses with a seating capacity of 24 or more, counting the driver's seat.

questions.q: Which Texas license class covers an ordinary passenger car or pickup?
options: Class M
Class A
Class C
questions.explain: Class C covers vehicles and combinations not included in Class A or B, which includes ordinary cars and light trucks.

questions.q: Which Texas license class is required to operate a motorcycle?
options: Class M
Class B
Class C
questions.explain: A Class M license authorizes the holder to operate a motorcycle.

questions.q: A teen driver must complete the Impact Texas Teen Drivers (ITTD) program within how many days before taking the driving test?
options: 1 year
90 days
30 days
questions.explain: DPS requires teens to finish the ITTD program within 90 days of their driving skills test.
questions.source: Texas DPS, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

questions.q: Who must complete the Impact Texas Adult Drivers (ITAD) program before the driving test?
options: Drivers aged 18 to 24 who must take an adult driver education course
Every driver over 65 renewing a license
Only commercial truck drivers
questions.explain: DPS requires the one-hour ITAD video for 18- to 24-year-olds who are required to complete adult driver education.
questions.source: Texas DPS, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program

questions.q: What is the main focus of the Impact Texas Drivers program?
options: How to change a flat tire
How to register a vehicle
The dangers of distracted driving
questions.explain: DPS describes the ITD program as education about the risks and consequences of distracted driving.
questions.source: Texas DPS, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program

questions.q: Texas generally will not issue a first driver license to a person younger than ___ years old without a driver education certificate.
questions.explain: Applicants under 25 must submit a driver education certificate, unless they hold a valid license from another state.

questions.q: A 20-year-old moving to Texas has a valid driver license from another state. Must they take a Texas driver education course?
options: Yes, but only the classroom portion
No, the driver education requirement does not apply to holders of a valid out-of-state license
Yes, everyone under 25 must take it
questions.explain: The under-25 driver education rule does not apply to someone who holds a valid driver license issued by another state.

questions.q: Before getting a provisional license, how many hours of behind-the-wheel practice must a teen complete, and how many at night?
options: 30 hours, with at least 10 at night
20 hours, with at least 5 at night
50 hours, with none required at night
questions.explain: DPS lists 30 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, including at least 10 at night, with a licensed driver 21 or older in the car.
questions.source: Texas DPS, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

questions.q: For one license application and fee, how many tries does a Texas applicant get to pass each part of the exam?
options: Five
One
Three
questions.explain: An applicant is entitled to three attempts at each examination element per application; after that, a new application and fee are needed.
